protocol.name: htm_shell_v1
protocol.description:
This protocol assigns an authorized HTMShell controller a semantic shell-root role on an ordinary wl_surface. Surface content, buffers, damage, frame callbacks, output information, and input continue to use standard Wayland protocols.
Version 1 is an experimental feasibility contract. It is not a standard and is not part of wayland-protocols. The v1 suffix names this experimental protocol family; normal Wayland interface versions govern additive wire evolution. No separate protocol-major or protocol-minor exchange exists.

interface.name: htm_shell_manager_v1
interface.description:
The manager grants shell-root authority to one authorized client. The authenticate request is a provisional development bootstrap mechanism, not a commitment to a production authentication policy.
A compositor must withhold shell authority until authorization succeeds. Authorization is scoped to the Wayland client connection and disappears when that connection is destroyed. A production compositor is expected to enforce authorization through compositor or session policy, preferably by withholding this privileged global from clients without shell authority.

entry.name: unauthorized
entry.summary: authorization failed or was not completed

entry.name: controller_exists
entry.summary: another client already controls HTMShell roots

entry.name: invalid_surface
entry.summary: the surface is invalid or already has a role

entry.name: invalid_output
entry.summary: the output is invalid or unavailable

entry.name: duplicate_root
entry.summary: the surface already owns an HTMShell root

enum.name: capability
enum.description: Capability identifiers describe contract semantics, never compositor implementation details. Unknown values must be ignored by clients. A version 1 baseline implementation must advertise both root_overlay and standard_pointer_focus before ready. Future optional capabilities do not weaken these baseline requirements.

entry.name: standard_pointer_focus
entry.summary: shell roots participate in normal Wayland pointer targeting

enum.name: role
enum.description: Roles specify desktop semantics rather than a render stage or numeric z-index. Version 1 defines only the overlay role. When several overlay roots share an output, later get_root requests are placed above earlier requests without crossing secure compositor ordering boundaries.

entry.name: overlay
entry.summary: above ordinary applications and below secure lock content

request.name: authenticate
request.description: The token is an opaque, single-session test capability. A production authorization mechanism may instead restrict global visibility, inherit authority from the compositor, or use session-manager integration. This request remains solely to exercise the development reference host and may be removed by a breaking experimental revision before stabilization.

request.name: get_root
request.description: This request permanently assigns a shell-root role to surface. The role remains attached to the wl_surface for its lifetime, even after the root object is destroyed. The client must not attach a buffer until it has acknowledged the initial configure event. The surface must not already have another role or an attached buffer. Output association and role are immutable for the root lifetime.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroying this object does not destroy roots already created by this client. Client disconnection always revokes controller authority and destroys all associated roots.

event.name: capability
event.description: This event is sent after successful authorization and before ready. Capability events must not be sent after ready for this manager object.

event.name: ready
event.description: After this event, the client may create roots using advertised roles. Exactly one ready event is sent after successful authorization.

interface.name: htm_shell_root_v1
interface.description:
The root owns semantic placement for one wl_surface on one wl_output. The compositor chooses its internal scene placement. The client continues to use wl_surface requests for content and standard seat objects for input.
If the associated wl_output global is removed, the compositor immediately unmaps the root and removes it from input targeting. The client destroys the root after receiving wl_registry.global_remove for that output. Until then the root is inert and commits cannot remap it.

entry.name: invalid_ack
entry.summary: the configure serial is unknown or stale

entry.name: buffer_before_ack
entry.summary: a buffer was committed before the initial configure ack

entry.name: invalid_size
entry.summary: committed surface dimensions exceed implementation limits

request.name: ack_configure
request.description: The client acknowledges that subsequent surface state is based on this configure. A client must acknowledge the initial configure before attaching its first buffer. When multiple configure events are pending, acknowledging the newest serial also acknowledges earlier configures. An unknown serial, an already acknowledged serial, or a serial older than the most recently acknowledged configure is invalid.

request.name: destroy
request.description: The compositor must immediately remove the root from presentation and input targeting. The wl_surface keeps its permanent role and cannot be reused for an incompatible role. Destroying the wl_surface first causes the compositor to destroy the corresponding root resource. Destroying the root first leaves the wl_surface alive but permanently role-bound.

event.name: configure
event.description: Width and height are output-local logical dimensions. Buffer scale and fractional-scale behavior use existing Wayland protocols. Both values are positive. A configure does not take effect until acknowledged and a corresponding wl_surface state is committed.
